beats.event: Harishchandra reigns as a beloved and prosperous truth-loving king
A hunting illusion draws him into disrupting Vishvamitra's meditation
He apologizes and promises the sage any boon he asks
Vishvamitra claims the entire kingdom as dakshina
He surrenders throne, wealth, even his royal clothes
Vishvamitra curses the five guardian deities who condemned Harishchandra
Wanders with wife Shaivya and son Rohitashva to holy Kashi
To pay the sage he sells his wife and son as slaves
The sage still demands more; the sale money is not enough
He sells himself to a chandala at the cremation ground
Collects burning-fees among the dead as the chandala's slave
His son Rohitashva dies of a snakebite in the forest
His wife brings the body; he demands the cremation fee from her
The gods appear with Vishvamitra; the whole ordeal was a test
He refuses heaven without his people; Indra grants their ascent
Harishchandra and his subjects rise together into heaven
